clue.text: See 18
Take aroma off line

blocks.note: first meaning: to ..., removing a smell from something
second meaning: ancestry, as in a family line

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip the smell from a washing line, or a line of perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as DE-SCENT, a coinage meaning remove the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent is lineage or ancestry, the sense in which a family line passes down through generations.

clue.text: A rock film that's not especially big on the lens

indicators.note: 'not big' tells us the two words that follow are each cut short, losing their final letter

blocks.note: very, a synonym for especially, without its last letter
surface padding, part of the 'not big' signal that shortens the words
a glass is a lens, as in a magnifying glass, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A rock documentary that isn't much of a feature for camera buffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock film' suggests a music movie; here it is a thin film of ice glazing rock. 'Big' and 'on the' just pad the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Verglas is the thin transparent coating of ice that forms on rocks and roads, a filmlike glaze.

clue.text: This is On the Beach - long song about dictator

indicators.note: about means going around, so the long song wraps itself around the dictator

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for long
an aria is an operatic song
Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator

explanation.surface: A description of a long track on a record called On the Beach, about a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: On the Beach looks like the title of a novel or album; it is literally where kelp washes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminaria is a genus of kelp, the large brown seaweed commonly found stranded along the shoreline.

clue.text: Instructions for Alice helping with (growth) treatment

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so the answer is a portion taken out of the following word

blocks.note: surface padding, a nod to what the cake does to Alice
the letters sit inside this word, after its first two

explanation.surface: Guidance given to a patient called Alice about a course of medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland a small cake bears a label of two words telling her to consume it, and it makes her grow enormously.
explanation.definitionFit: The words on the Wonderland cake are a direct command telling Alice to consume it, so they are her instructions.

clue.text: Ban doctor boarding ship carrying drug

blocks.note: E is ecstasy
MB, Bachelor of Medicine
the Argo, Jason's ship

explanation.surface: A medic is barred after getting on a vessel smuggling narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue the doctor sits on top of the ship, and the drug is carried at the head of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, typically on trade with a particular country.

clue.text: T.S. Eliot's randomly assigned figure of speech

indicators.note: letters assigned at random end up in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the poet's name, initials included

explanation.surface: A rhetorical device that the poet T.S. Eliot was handed by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, like 'not bad', a classic rhetorical device.

clue.text: See 15
Spirit appears after Jack's topped off stage

indicators.note: having its top taken off means the first letter is lost

blocks.note: Jack Frost, personification of wintry weather
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack drank so much spirit that he fell off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack's topped' reads as Jack being killed; Jack Frost loses his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor, so a stage in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Her thanks somewhat hard to accept?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first word holds the rest inside it

blocks.note: ta is informal British thanks
a bit, slightly
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman whose gratitude seems a little grudging.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Her' is a woman's name, not a pronoun to be explained.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a female given name, so it can stand for one particular woman referred to as her.

clue.text: See 15
Citadel's grand opening denied agent of mischief when £1,000 is put forward

indicators.note: the opening letter, which happens to be G for grand, is refused entry

blocks.note: K is a thousand, as in a grand
a gremlin is an imaginary sprite blamed for mechanical faults

explanation.surface: A fortress's gala opening is refused to a troublemaker until he pays a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand and £1,000 mean the same, so G at the front is swapped for K.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex in Moscow; the Russian word kreml means a citadel.

clue.text: Inverted arrival is integral to dumb mistake

indicators.note: being integral to something means being built into it, so one part sits inside the other
turned upside down in a down-reading sense, so the whole result is read backwards

blocks.note: mute means unable to speak
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: Getting the order of arrivals upside down is a stupid error.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, often listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Formal attire covers shirt on this chap's back

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, enclosing it
'is back' says the result is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: a suit is formal clothing
a T-shirt, cut to its letter

explanation.surface: A man's formal jacket is draped over the shirt on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about clothes, but 'this chap's back' means the name is SUTIT reversed: TITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is a man's name, so it names the particular fellow the clue points to as this chap.

clue.text: Select retreats in French grounds - such will do for deserters?

indicators.note: something that retreats goes backwards, so the word runs the other way
in places the reversed word inside the French word

blocks.note: opt means choose
raison is French for reason, grounds for something

explanation.surface: An elite force withdraws to French territory, a fate fit for army deserters.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are proverbially the first to desert a sinking ship, so the deserters are rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison laid for vermin kills rats, the creatures famous for abandoning sinking ships, hence deserters.

clue.text: Break or make: he bet more than that on black and won

annotation.answer: THE MAN WHO AT MONTE CARLO BROKE THE BANK

definitions.text: Break or make: he bet more than that on black and won

blocks.note: surface: the phrase make or break, a decisive moment for a gambler

blocks.clueFragment: he bet more than that on black and won
blocks.note: setter's reading: a famous gambler who staked heavily at roulette and cleaned out the casino

explanation.surface: A make-or-break moment at the roulette table where a gambler bets big on black and wins.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of an 1892 music-hall song about a gambler who drained a casino table's reserve; 'break' is the sense used of a bank in gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's title names a gambler who won so much that a roulette table ran out of chips, a famous casino coup.

clue.text: Ordered chiefs of Taxes, Customs and Excise to dry up!

indicators.note: chiefs are heads, so only the leading letter of each word is taken
ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
taken whole

explanation.surface: Heads of the tax authorities are told to stop the flow of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Customs and Excise was the British government department for duties, now merged into HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: To exsiccate is to dry something out completely, a formal word for drying up moisture.

clue.text: Tinned pork's taken by elevated railroad to mountain plant

indicators.note: tinned food is sealed inside a can, so the meat goes inside the metal's symbol

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
pork is pig meat
the El is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Canned meat is carried up a mountain railway to feed the botanists.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is SN, its chemical symbol, and PIG goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel, also called baldmoney or meu, is an aromatic plant of the carrot family growing on mountain pastures.

clue.text: 15 7 10 almost cooked thoroughly without a daily to do the rounds

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so a final letter is dropped
doing the rounds means travelling round, so a letter moves round to the far end

blocks.note: a char is a daily cleaning lady, so without one is char-less
devilled food is cooked with hot spices
well means thoroughly, as in shake well

explanation.surface: A cryptic recipe: something nearly cooked through, with no cleaner, going on her rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the cooked word, and the doubled S at the end of the cleaner-free word travels round to the very end. A daily is British for a cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Deville Wells was the English fraudster who won fortunes at Monte Carlo in 1891 and inspired the song.

clue.text: Black can opener is mislaid

indicators.note: losing the opener means the first letter goes missing

blocks.note: he can means he is able

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured tin opener has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can opener' looks like a kitchen tool; 'can' is the verb, worth IS ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is black, both as the heraldic tincture name and in poetic use for dark colours.

clue.text: Round v-vessels containing silver substitute

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside
brought round means turned about, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: pots are vessels, and the stammer doubles the initial letter
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A stammered order for a round of silver vessels to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The stuttered 'v-' tells us to repeat the first letter of the vessels word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute used until something better is available.

clue.text: Shakespeare wants fabulous bird in principle!

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the name for Shakespeare

blocks.note: the Bard of Avon
the roc is a mythical giant bird

explanation.surface: Shakespeare would like a legendary bird, at least theoretically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' reads as a phrase meaning theoretically; 'in' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brocard is an elementary legal maxim or principle, a short rule cited in argument.

clue.text: Excitedly taking notes

blocks.note: surface: someone scribbling down notes in a frenzy
setter's reading: musicians taking up their notes in a passage played excitedly

explanation.surface: A student jotting down a lecture in a feverish rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes are musical notes being played, and the answer is the score marking that tells the player to do so excitedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is an Italian musical direction meaning play in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Shot in the eye!

blocks.note: first meaning: the pub device that measures out a shot of spirits
second meaning: relating to the eye or vision

explanation.walkthrough: An Optic is a British trade name for the measure fixed to an upturned spirits bottle in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye or sight, and in pubs it names the dispenser for a measured shot.

clue.text: Mixed aromas embellish love for full-bodied Spanish female

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Blended scents add romance to a rich Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Full-bodied hints at amoroso sherry; the feminine form gives a Spanish lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorosa is Spanish for a woman in love, a sweetheart, echoing the rich sherry style amoroso.

clue.text: Maybe Edward VI's knight holds fire

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside

blocks.note: KT is the abbreviation for knight
an ingle is a fire on a hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: The boy king's knight keeps a fire burning.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward VI came to the throne aged nine, so 'Maybe' marks him as an example of a young king.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinglet is a minor or petty king; a boy monarch like Edward VI is an example.

clue.text: Cry about a great flier

indicators.note: about means going around something

blocks.note: a wail is a cry
taken as written
GT is short for great

explanation.surface: A shout goes up about a magnificent pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great flier' looks like an aviator; the flier is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagtail is a small slender bird, so it is a creature that flies through the air.

clue.text: About to waste credit, get caught short

indicators.note: about means placed around the other words

blocks.note: copped is slang for caught by the police
to lose is to waste, as in lose time
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A spendthrift is told they're about to blow their credit and be left short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads like running out of money; 'short' is the haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-cropped hair is cut very short, close to the scalp.
